items.notes: Quote: "A handler or middleware awaits `c.req.formData()` and then `c.req.parseBody()` on a multipart or urlencoded POST"; "Multipart: parseBody throws 'no boundary found in multipart body' and the route returns 500. Urlencoded: it returns an object keyed by a generated multipart boundary"; the Fix names the mechanism: "always calling `arrayBuffer()`, which re-serializes a cached FormData with a new boundary". This recovers GT-p1. Proposed change: "when the request is a `HonoRequest`, reuse `request.formData()` (which honours `bodyCache.formData`) and apply the media-type normalization only when parsing raw bytes". That fixes the formData()->parseBody() order. However, it routes every HonoRequest through request.formData(). If text()/arrayBuffer()/blob() was cached first, #cachedBody (src/request.ts:228-235) returns new Response(body).formData() with no Content-Type. That is the base behaviour, which the register records as failing with 500, so the change regresses orders that work at head and that the required_outcome says must keep working. First-read HonoRequests would also skip the PR's normalization and depend on native Request.formData() being case-insensitive (true on Node 24, which I checked; not established for other runtimes). Partial.

Quote: "`methodOverride` still guards its form parsing with case-sensitive `startsWith('multipart/form-data')` and `startsWith('application/x-www-form-urlencoded')`, so mixed-case media types skip the override; the issue names only parseBody and validator." Accurate: src/middleware/method-override/index.ts:74 and :92 use case-sensitive startsWith. The file is untouched by this PR and the behaviour predates it. The item flags only that the PR's scope is incomplete, as the reviewer notes by pointing out that the issue covers just parseBody and validator. It is a follow-up observation, not a defect this change introduces.

Quote: "A handler awaits `c.req.formData()` and then `c.req.parseBody()` on a multipart or urlencoded POST, leaving only `bodyCache.formData` populated" ... "`parseFormData()` now calls `arrayBuffer()`, which re-serializes the cached FormData with a new boundary; it is then parsed with the original Content-Type. Multipart throws `Failed to parse body as FormData.` (500); urlencoded returns a garbage key". This is exactly GT-p1's trigger, mechanism (src/utils/body.ts:125-126 arrayBuffer() + bufferToFormData with original Content-Type; src/request.ts:228-235 #cachedBody re-serializing via new Response(body)[key]()) and the multipart and urlencoded manifestations. Fix: "reuse `request.bodyCache.formData` when it is already set, and only take the `arrayBuffer()` and `bufferToFormData` path when it is not" plus a regression test. That is the register's upstream approach: it restores correct fields for both content types, removes the cache overwrite, and leaves first read and text/arrayBuffer/blob/validator-before-parseBody orders on the existing arrayBuffer path. Sufficient.

Quote: "Codecov reported 76.47% patch coverage, with three uncovered lines in `src/utils/body.ts` and one in `src/utils/buffer.ts`." Accurate (packet section 6: body.ts 3 missing, buffer.ts 1 missing), but the register's non_defects rule that coverage hygiene alone is non-material, and the item names no failing behaviour.

Quote: "A handler or middleware calls `await c.req.formData()` and then `await c.req.parseBody()` ... with no arrayBuffer cached, `HonoRequest#cachedBody` re-serializes the cached FormData into a new multipart body with a fresh boundary, which is parsed against the original Content-Type"; consequence "Multipart requests make `parseBody()` reject with `TypeError: Failed to parse body as FormData.`; urlencoded requests silently return garbage keys such as `------formdata-undici-...`". Same trigger, mechanism and manifestations as GT-p1 (src/utils/body.ts:125-126, src/request.ts:228-235). Fix: "when the request is a `HonoRequest` with `bodyCache.formData` set, await that value (as `src/validator/validator.ts` does) before falling back to `arrayBuffer()` and `bufferToFormData`". That is the register's upstream approach (validator.ts:115-121 does the same). It restores both content types, stops the cache overwrite, and leaves the other orders on the existing path. Sufficient.

Quote: "After `parseBody()` the first `bodyCache` key is now `arrayBuffer` rather than `formData`, so `c.req.text()`, `c.req.json()` and `cloneRawRequest` read the raw bytes afterwards, and the multipart bytes stay cached for the request lifetime." This is accurate: parseFormData calls arrayBuffer() first, which caches it through #cachedBody, and cloneRawRequest (src/request.ts:481) uses Object.keys(bodyCache)[0]. It asserts no failure; reading the original bytes is correct, if anything better than re-serializing. Keeping the buffer cached is a memory observation with no demonstrated consequence (the register's non_defects also rule out a doubled-memory claim). Below the finding threshold.
